chapter: The Footlight Club and Washington friends
title: Sammy Woods and Roy Eldridge strolling with a joint; reefer songs
summary: Guitarist Sammy Woods taught him chords, and he recalls Roy Eldridge and Woods playing in the streets while smoking marijuana, plus Cab Calloway's Reefer Man.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: There was this guitar player that worked with Booker Coleman and taught me a lot about chords; his name was Sammy Woods. Just to show you how things change, and different... Roy Eldridge used to come to Washington here. When he was in town, Sammy would have his guitar, and he'd have a string around his neck, and he would go around and see Roy. Between shows, Roy would come out with his horn and a mute. And they would walk, like... The Howard Theatre was at Wilberg(?) and T Street, which is between Sixth and Seventh. Well, when you walk around Sixth Street, it's just residential. And Sammy and Roy... Roy would get his horn and his mute, and Sammy with his guitar, and they would walk around there through the streets and smoke a joint, and they'd play, he strumming the guitar and Roy playing... They'd walk through the street, and nobody paid any attention to anybody. Smoking pot was just something nobody paid any attention to. They'd do it right on

the streets of downtown Washington, if you wanted to. I guess if people had knowledgeable, they might have said something. There were a lot of times things said about "people who smoke reefers are crazy" and all that, but that's about as far as it went. People sang songs about it...
Yes. You know, "Reefer Man." Cab Calloway sang "Reefer Man." He had a thing about "a reefer five feet long."
Anyway, things like that were happening. And these guys that I knew, like Sammy Woods and Leonard Phillips...
